Code agents represent one of the most significant breakthroughs in artificial intelligence applications to date. Red-teaming, in the context of AI systems, involves systematically probing models with adversarial inputs and edge cases to identify failure modes, safety gaps, and security vulnerabilities. For code agents, this involves testing with malicious prompts, ambiguous specifications, edge-case requirements, and attempts to elicit insecure code generation. The field is still nascent, with many challenges remaining in developing standardized red-teaming methodologies for code agents.
